GenerateMoveStateMachine.rationale: C# (Myte.cs:46-62): TOXIC -> BITE -> SUCK -> TOXIC, plus a ConditionalBranchState 'INIT_MOVE' with AddState(TOXIC, SlotName == 'first') then AddState(SUCK, SlotName == 'second'); initialState = the conditional branch. myte.py:51-57 reproduces the ring, both conditional branches in the same order and the same initial state. Note the Myte has NO 'third' arm, so a Myte in any other slot would hit ConditionalBranchState.GetNextState's throw (seam step 26) on both sides - and MytesNormal.cs:14 declares exactly two slots.

guards.what: C# leaves INIT_MOVE out of the registered state list; the sim registers it
guards.rationale: Myte.cs:58-61 adds only TOXIC, BITE and SUCK to `list` and then passes conditionalBranchState as the initialState, so INIT_MOVE is never handed to MonsterMoveStateMachine's RegisterStates loop (MonsterMoveStateMachine.cs:22-25). myte.py:57 passes [toxic, bite, suck, init]. Harmless on both sides: registration is only consulted to resolve an id RETURNED by a GetNextState (MonsterMoveStateMachine.cs:64-75, seam step 23/31), and nothing returns 'INIT_MOVE' - the initial state is held by reference, and a branch never appears in StateLog (ShouldAppearInLogs is false, seam step 6), so the one-entry initial log (seam step 28) is empty on both sides too. This is the sim being MORE permissive, not differently behaved.

guards.what: slot names and the two-Myte encounter
guards.rationale: MytesNormal.cs:14 Slots = [first, second] and :33-38 generates two Mytes in that order; MytesEncounter.create_monsters (myte.py:81-82) returns [Myte(slot='first'), Myte(slot='second')]. The C# predicate reads Creature.SlotName, the sim reads self.slot set by the same encounter.

Bug class 18 checked. Myte.cs:66-74's `if (TestMode.IsOff)` arm is the SHIPPING arm and it contains only NMyteVfx.SetTarget - a vfx aim. There is no alternate mechanical arm to have ported the wrong half of.

guards.what: TOXIC puts its cards in the HAND, not the discard
guards.rationale: Myte.cs:77 CardPileCmd.AddToCombatAndPreview<Toxic>(targets, PileType.Hand, 2, null); myte.py:62-63 loops twice over CardPileCmd.add_to_hand. Worth its own entry because the batch's other status-card move (Chomper's SCREECH) targets PileType.Discard, and the two ports correctly differ.

BiteDamage (DeadlyEnemies, 15, 13) -> 13; SuckDamage (DeadlyEnemies, 6, 4) -> 4; SuckStrength (DeadlyEnemies, 3, 2) -> 2; _toxicCount = 2 (Myte.cs:24, 38-42). Sim _BITE_DMG=13, _SUCK_DMG=4, _SUCK_STR=2, _TOXIC_COUNT=2. SuckMove damages then applies Strength to itself; myte.py:68-72 keeps the order.
Myte.cs overrides no AfterAddedToRoom and the sim's Myte.__init__ applies no power (myte.py:33-40 only stores the slot), so SHARED-FINDINGS section 2 does not apply to this unit at all.
